title: Rav Mari bar Hama
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Arakhin 21a, where he raised a difficulty against Rav Hisda. Hyman suggests that perhaps בר״ח was originally written, meaning “son of Rav Hisda,” and from this “bar Hama” came to be.[^1][^2]

notes.text: כא. gives 21a by convention without fresh verification.

Hyman explicitly supplies bar Rav Hisda as the proposed expansion of בר״ח; this is his conjecture about an original abbreviation, not an attested correction history or title guessed by the translator. The natural questioner is Mari and addressee Hisda. All three full רב occurrences remain Rav; Hama is untitled.
